newTerms.spirit livers: los que viven en el espíritu

forcedChoices.reason: The English does not give the gender of the servant of Karuska; Spanish forces one, and the masculine is the generic form.

forcedChoices.choice: tú for Norana to Peter, Thomas, and Simon
forcedChoices.reason: One person speaks to one person; no sign of the great respect that calls for usted.
The feminine 'perra' is an insult with a sexual sense in much of the Spanish-speaking world; the masculine keeps the image of the dogs at the table.
Norana speaks to all the disciples present ('before them all', 'You are not worthy to be his disciples').
Jesus answers the question of Nathaniel; the 'you' can also be general, but the context is the answer to one person.
Here 'actual' is the plain word, not the glossary term 'actual' (en acto); 'actual' in Spanish is a false friend.
The thoughts restate answers to the apostles and evangelists as a group; the packet asks for ustedes when the text speaks to the reader.
Spanish dates take no ordinal suffix; the tag is kept so the HTML stays the same as the English.
Spanish puts the era after the year; the small-caps span moves with it.
